Improve Freight Planning with Predictive Transport Management

Thematic Area: Intelligent Transport Planning & Route Prediction

How might we use an AI-powered transport-management system with route prediction to improve freight planning and delivery performance?

Background

A shipping and logistics group wants to automate transport planning within its freight-forwarding business. It needs a transport-management system (TMS) that combines operational records with predictive route analysis to support planning decisions.

The objective is to organise transport work, anticipate route conditions and improve the use of vehicles and delivery resources. Relevant startups offer transport-management software, logistics optimisation, mapping and location analytics.

The solution should connect with existing systems and reflect shipment requirements and operating constraints.

Significance of Problem

Key challenges include:

  • Higher transport costs: Inefficient routes and resource allocation increase travel and operating expenses.
  • Less reliable delivery plans: Limited visibility of route performance makes delivery schedules harder to maintain.
  • Slower planning: Comparing routes, assigning resources and responding to disruptions require significant planning effort.

Existing Efforts

  • Available capabilities: A logistics software provider offers delivery-order management, route optimisation, driver assignment, tracking and electronic POD. A mapping provider offers traffic and distance analysis, delivery heatmaps and disruption-aware route planning.
  • Collaboration focus: Integrate route prediction into the TMS, connect the required operational and mapping data, and present recommendations within the planner’s workflow. Compare planning effort, distance, delivery performance and operating costs against the current approach.

Potential Market Size

  • Transport-management systems: The global market was estimated at US$18.6 billion in 2025 and is forecast to reach US$68.4 billion by 2033, with 17.9% annual growth during 2026–2033.
  • Regional growth: Asia Pacific is forecast to be the fastest-growing TMS region during 2026–2033, supporting opportunities for solutions serving Indonesian logistics operations.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
